chapter.li: Verse25 After Abinadi had finished saying this, he asked them: Have 2PP you taught these people to take care to do all these things, to keep these commandments? VerseEnd Verse26 I tell 2PP you: No. Because if 2PP you had, the Lord wouldn’t have had me come and prophesy evil about this people. VerseEnd Verse27 Now 2PP you’ve said that salvation comes by the Law of Moses. I tell 2PP you, while it’s still necessary for 2PP you to keep the Law of Moses, the time will come when it won’t be necessary to keep it anymore. VerseEnd Verse28 Furthermore, I declare that salvation doesn’t come by the Law alone. If it weren’t for the atonement God Himself will make for His people’s sins and iniquities, they would unavoidably perish, despite the Law of Moses. VerseEnd Verse29 2PP You should understand that it was necessary for there to be a very strict law given to the Israelites. They were a stubborn people, quick to commit iniquity and slow to remember the Lord who is God. VerseEnd Verse30 So a law of performances and ordinances was given to them, one they were to strictly follow on a daily basis to remind them of God and their duty toward Him. VerseEnd Verse31 But I tell 2PP you all these things symbolized what was to come. VerseEnd

Verse32 Now, did they understand the Law? I tell 2PP you: No, not all of them understood the Law — because of the hardness of their hearts. They didn’t understand that no one could be saved except through God’s redemption. VerseEnd Verse33 Didn’t Moses prophesy to them about the coming Messiah and that God would redeem His people? Yes, and even all the prophets that have prophesied ever since the world began, haven’t they spoken more or less about these things? VerseEnd Verse34 Haven’t they said that God Himself would come down among mankind and take upon Himself the form of a man and go about in great power on the earth? VerseEnd Verse35 And haven’t they also said He would enable the resurrection of the dead and that He Himself would be oppressed and afflicted? VerseEnd

LEChapter14 Verse1 Of course, doesn’t Isaiah say: Who believes what we’ve heard? Who’s heard the Lord’s revelation? VerseEnd Verse2 For He’ll grow up with His favor like a lively vine springing from the desert ground. He has no rank or position deserving respect, and when we notice Him, there’s nothing about Him to please us. VerseEnd Verse3 He is despised and rejected by men — a man of sorrow and familiar with disease. And we turned our faces away, ignoring Him. He was despised and thought to be of no value. VerseEnd Verse4 Yet it was our sickness He took upon Himself, our suffering He endured. VerseEnd

Verse5 He suffered for our sins, healed our sickness; was punished for our iniquities, bearing our guilt to completely restore us. VerseEnd Verse6 We all strayed like sheep, wandering off — each one going their own way; and the Lord has imposed on Him the guilt belonging to us all. VerseEnd Verse7 He was oppressed and submitted, without complaining; like a lamb brought to be slaughtered, and as a ewe is silent while they shear her, so He endured without opening His mouth. VerseEnd Verse8 He was condemned by an unjust judgment. There were none who defended Him. For He was slain as a sacrifice for the transgressions of My people, who deserved the punishment. VerseEnd Verse9 He died with the wicked, and was buried with the rich. Though He had done no evil, nor had He declared anything untrue; VerseEnd Verse10 but the Lord was content with His offering; satisfied with His healing.

After He made himself a sin offering, He’ll inherit offspring, obtain eternal life, and vindicate God’s promises. VerseEnd Verse11 He’ll see His sacrifice and will be satisfied; by the understanding He gains, the righteous Servant will make many others righteous, for He’ll remove their iniquities. VerseEnd Verse12 Therefore I intend for Him to inherit multitudes, and His triumph will endow Him eternally — because He submitted willingly to death, and He was regarded as a sinner; but instead, He took on other’s guilt while making intercession for sinners. VerseEnd

LEChapter15 Verse1 Then Abinadi said to them: I want 2PP you to understand that God Himself will come down among mankind and redeem His people. VerseEnd Verse2 And because He’ll dwell in the flesh, He’ll be called the Son of God. He’ll subject the flesh to the Father’s will, gaining the role of the Father and the Son: VerseEnd Verse3 the Father because He was conceived by God’s power and the Son because of the flesh, becoming the Father and Son in this way. VerseEnd Verse4 And they’re united as one God — indeed, the very Eternal Father of heaven and earth. VerseEnd Verse5 So the flesh becomes subject to the Spirit, or the Son to the Father, being one God, suffering temptation and not yielding to it, but allowing Himself to be mocked, whipped, thrown out, and disowned by His people. VerseEnd

Verse6 After all this, and after performing many mighty miracles among mankind, He’ll be led, just as Isaiah said, as a ewe is silent while they shear her, so He endured without opening His mouth. VerseEnd Verse7 Yes, He’ll be led, crucified, and killed, the mortal flesh fully surrendering to death, the Son’s will submitting entirely to the Father’s will. VerseEnd Verse8 And so God breaks the chains of death, gaining victory over death, giving the Son power to make intercession for mankind, VerseEnd Verse9 having ascended into heaven, showing tender mercy, being filled with compassion toward mankind, standing between them and justice, having conquered death, Himself assuming responsibility for their transgressions and iniquity, having redeemed them, and satisfied the demands of justice. VerseEnd

Verse10 Now I ask 2PP you: Who will identify His sons and daughters? I tell 2PP you that after His life has been made a sin offering, He’ll reclaim His children. Now, what do 2PP you say? Who will be His children? VerseEnd Verse11 I tell 2PP you that whoever has believed the prophet’s words — moreover, all the holy prophets who have prophesied about the Lord’s coming, I tell 2PP you that all those who have followed their words and believed that the Lord would redeem His people and have looked forward to that day for a remission of their sins, I tell 2PP you that these are His children, or they are heirs of God’s kingdom. VerseEnd Verse12 These are the ones whose sins He has borne; these are the ones He has died for, to redeem them from their transgressions. And now, are they not His children? VerseEnd Verse13 And the prophets, every one who’s proclaimed His messages, who hasn’t fallen into transgression — I mean all the holy prophets since the world began — I tell 2PP you that they are His children. VerseEnd Verse14 These are the ones announcing good news, that proclaim peace, that report coming good fortune, announcing victory, telling Zion: 2PSI Your God reigns! VerseEnd Verse15 How welcome on the mountain are their footsteps! VerseEnd Verse16 And how welcome on the mountain are the footsteps of those who are still announcing victory! VerseEnd Verse17 Again, how welcome on the mountain are the footsteps of those who will continue announcing victory from now on and forever! VerseEnd

Verse18 I tell 2PP you: This isn’t all. Again, how welcome on the mountain are the footsteps of Him who brings good news and is the Founder of peace — meaning, the Lord who’s redeemed and granted His people salvation. VerseEnd Verse19 If it weren’t for the redemption He has made for His people, which was planned from the start of creation, I say that if it weren’t for this — all mankind would be doomed. VerseEnd Verse20 But the chains of death will be broken. And the Son’s authority includes power over the dead; therefore He owns the resurrection of the dead. VerseEnd Verse21 And a resurrection is coming, that is a first resurrection, of those who have lived, now live, and will live, up until the resurrection of Christ (and that is His name). VerseEnd Verse22 Now the resurrection of all the prophets and those who have believed their messages — or those who have kept God’s commandments — are the ones who will come forth in the first resurrection; therefore that is the initial resurrection. VerseEnd Verse23 They’re raised to live with God, who’s redeemed them. So they have eternal life through the Messiah, who’s broken the chains of death. VerseEnd

Verse24 And those who have died in ignorance before the Messiah came, not having salvation taught to them, are also included in the first resurrection. So the Lord brings about their restoration, and they’re included as part of the first resurrection, or have eternal life, being redeemed by the Lord. VerseEnd Verse25 And little children also have eternal life. VerseEnd

Verse26 However, beware and be fearful of God’s judgment of 2PP you — as 2PP you should — because the Lord doesn’t redeem anyone who rebels against Him and dies in their sins. Understand that everyone, from the beginning, who deliberately refuses to follow God while knowing His commandments, won’t be redeemed by Him. These people don’t have any part in the first resurrection. VerseEnd Verse27 Therefore shouldn’t 2PP you be afraid? Because the Lord hasn’t redeemed anyone like that, and salvation doesn’t come to anyone like that. And He can’t redeem them either, for He can’t go back on His word or deny justice when it applies. VerseEnd

Verse28 Now I tell 2PP you that the time will come when the Lord’s salvation will be declared to all people of every nation, tribe, and language. VerseEnd Verse29 Listen, 2PP your border guards shout out together their joyful praise, for everyone will witness the Lord’s return to Zion. VerseEnd Verse30 Everyone will proclaim together, O ruins of Jerusalem! The Lord now comforts 2PP you His people, coming to redeem Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse31 The Lord will bare His holy arm in the sight of every nation, and all will see God’s victory to the very end of the earth. VerseEnd

LEChapter16 Verse1 After Abinadi had spoken these words, he reached out his arms and said: The time will come when everyone will see the Lord’s salvation, when all people of every nation, tribe, and language will see with their own eyes and acknowledge before God that His judgments are correct. VerseEnd Verse2 Then the wicked will be thrown out, and they’ll have a reason to howl, weep, wail, and grind their teeth — because they wouldn’t hearken to the Lord’s voice. Therefore the Lord won’t redeem them. VerseEnd Verse3 Because they’re carnal and devilish; and the accuser has power over them. Indeed, that old snake who deceived our first parents, which was the cause of their fall, resulting in mankind becoming carnal, sensual, devilish, knowing evil from good, and subjecting themselves to the accuser. VerseEnd Verse4 All mankind was then lost and they would have been permanently lost if God hadn’t redeemed His people from their lost and fallen state. VerseEnd Verse5 But remember that those who persist in their own carnal nature and follow sin and rebellion against God will remain in their fallen state, and the accuser has influence over them. So they’re as if no redemption had been made — effectively enemies of God; and the accuser is clearly an enemy of God. VerseEnd

Verse6 Now if the Messiah had not come into the world — speaking of future events as if they had already happened — there would have been no redemption. VerseEnd Verse7 And if the Messiah hadn’t risen from the dead or broken the chains of death — so that the grave had no victory and death no bite — there would have been no resurrection. VerseEnd Verse8 But there is a resurrection. Therefore the grave doesn’t have any victory, and death’s bite is swallowed up through the Messiah. VerseEnd Verse9 He is the light and life of the world, an endless light that can never be darkened and an endless life so there is no more death. VerseEnd Verse10 This mortal body will become immortal, and our decaying flesh will become free from decay, and in our bodies we’ll stand before the judgment seat of God to be judged by Him. Judged based on our works, whether they’re good or evil: VerseEnd Verse11 if good, to the resurrection of endless life and happiness; and if evil, to the resurrection of endless damnation, handed over to the accuser, who has authority over the condemned, which is damnation. VerseEnd Verse12 They lived unworthy, selfish lives, never repenting and asking forgiveness from the Lord, although He was always ready to forgive; they refused His mercy. They ignored warnings about their iniquities, and they wouldn’t abandon them. And though they were commanded to repent, they refused to repent. VerseEnd

Verse13 Now shouldn’t 2PP you fear God’s judgment and repent of 2PP your sins? Remember, 2PP you can be saved only in and through the Messiah. VerseEnd Verse14 Therefore if 2PP you teach the Law of Moses, also teach that it foreshadows what’s coming. VerseEnd Verse15 Teach them that redemption comes through Christ the Lord, who is the very Eternal Father. Amen. VerseEnd
